subject: Request: temporary handshake latency exemption for streaming endpoint (time-to-first-token)
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@nebulasys.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebulasys.com, security@nebulasys.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming handshake & sustained rate — can we get a temporary SLA carveout for the POC?

Hi Chloe,

We're starting the Nebula POC next week and ran a few baseline tests. When we run streaming generation against the model variant you've recommended, the Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) for the first prompt is averaging ~320ms (95th ~460ms) over our 2k sample. Sustained throughput during steady generation is closer to 18 tokens/sec on our consumer-grade clients, which is under the 30 tps we expected.

For the POC we need an interim commitment so we can demo a live streaming experience to our product team. Specifically we're asking Redwood for a temporary exception to the hosted streaming SLA for the following window: 2027-05-01 to 2027-07-01, with a target TTFT <= 350ms (p95) and sustained >= 18 tokens/sec for the demo tier. We'll accept narrow carveouts (region: us-west) and a visibility requirement (daily token-level traces).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can approve this sort of short-lived adjustment, and what the operational controls/limits would be (dedicated pool, max concurrency, fallback to non-streaming)? I've attached a short sample of our trace profile (nebula_handshake_profile.csv).

Thanks — Julia
Julia Park
Head of Integrations, Nebula Systems
From: chloe.martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@nebulasys.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming handshake & sustained rate — can we get a temporary SLA carveout for the POC?

Hi Julia — thanks for the profile and the clear ask. Short answer: we can usually support short-lived, region-scoped SLA exceptions for POCs with a few operational conditions. Below is a proposed path and the limits we'd ask to attach.

Summary proposal (initial):
- Window: 2027-05-01 -> 2027-07-01 (90 days)
- Scope: Hosted streaming endpoint in us-west only
- TTFT target: p95 <= 350ms for the first token on cold sessions (require baseline traces)
- Sustained target: >= 18 tokens/sec for demo clients (max sustained concurrency capped per org)
- Controls: restrict to a dedicated dev pool with a concurrency cap (we propose 8 concurrent streams), automatic fallback to non-streaming (sync) if burst > cap, and daily token-level visibility to Nebula and Redwood.
- Observability: we'll provide token-level traces and cost breakdowns. Any regression beyond agreed thresholds will trigger a canary rollback.

Operational asks from Nebula:
- Confirm expected concurrent demo users (peak) and region routing rules
- Sign the short amendment (I attached a draft: proposed-exception-draft.docx)

I'll loop in Markus (ops) and Laura (contracts) to validate the carveout and sign-off on the constraints. If you're happy with the bullet points I can push this through legal/ops by Friday.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Streaming handshake & sustained rate — approval & operational constraints

Chloe / Laura — forwarding Julia's ask and Chloe's proposed terms. Key items for ops/legal review:
- 90-day, region-scoped exception for TTFT p95 350ms and sustained >=18 tps
- Dedicated dev pool + concurrency cap (8) and explicit fallback to non-streaming
- Daily trace sharing and rollback trigger on regressions

Questions for Laura: do we need an SLA credit schedule for this temporary carveout, or can we record it as an operational exemption tied to the POC paperwork? Also, confirm whether we can expose token-level traces to an external account without additional NDAs.

If legal is OK, ops can pre-provision the small dev pool and I can greenlight the timeline.

Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming handshake & sustained rate — exception confirmed (terms & next steps)

Julia — quick update following legal/ops review. We can approve the temporary, region-scoped exception for the Nebula POC under the following conditions (please review):

1) Period: 2027-05-01 to 2027-07-01 (inclusive).
2) Scope: Hosted streaming endpoint (us-west) only, demo tier (non-production).
3) TTFT commitment: p95 <= 350ms for the first token on cold sessions, measured by Redwood using token-level traces that both parties will share daily.

4) Sustained throughput: target >= 18 tokens/sec for demo clients. We will cap sustained throughput per-organization to protect production pools — initial cap: 8 concurrent streams per Nebula account.

5) Fallback policy: If sustained concurrency or token emission exceeds the cap or if TTFT p95 degrades >25% from baseline, Redwood will route affected sessions to the non-streaming endpoint (sync) until remediation.

6) Monitoring & rollback: Daily dashboards visible to Nebula; automatic canary rollback trigger on sustained regressions.

7) Costs & credits: Exception applies at the standard demo pricing; we do not provide SLA credits for this temporary carveout. Any extended or production-facing SLAs will require a dedicated capacity commitment and a separate contract.

8) Data & traces: We will share token-level traces for the duration of the POC. Nebula must confirm there are no additional NDAs preventing trace sharing.

If you accept these terms, sign the attached amendment and complete the DocuSign at: https://www.docusign.com/sign/NB-EXC-20270501. Ops will provision the dev pool on Monday (2027-05-03) and notify you when the endpoint is live.

Thanks — looking forward to the demo.
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-exception-draft.docx (draft amendment), nebula_handshake_profile.csv (sample traces)
